153: ## 5. Region-capture processing design
154: 
155: ### 5.1 PDF viewer and coordinate system
156: 
157: The viewer must support page navigation, zoom, pan, and one draggable/resizable rectangle.
158: 
159: Keep a single canonical geometry representation in PDF page user-space coordinates. The screen rectangle is only a visual representation. A conversion layer must account for:
160: 
161: - Current zoom.
162: - Pan/scroll offset.
163: - Page rotation.
164: - `CropBox` and `MediaBox` offsets.
165: - High-DPI and operating-system display scaling.
166: 
167: Normalize every rectangle so `x0 < x1` and `y0 < y1`; reject zero-area or out-of-page selections with a visible error. Store the canonical page-space rectangle with the preview/provenance.
168: 
169: Do not duplicate coordinate conversion logic in Slint callbacks, `dh-part3`, and the PDF renderer. The UI should report pointer positions and display geometry; a tested geometry layer should produce the page-space `BBox`.
170: 
171: ### 5.2 Full-page grid first
172: 
173: For the selected page, the extraction path should build or retrieve the page's digital table/cell grid before applying the selected rectangle.
174: 
175: Why: if the application only crops text to the rectangle first, it may not know that a cell extends outside the rectangle. Building the full-page grid first allows it to identify cells whose boundaries cross the selection edge.
176: 
177: The grid result should use the existing `TableBlock` and `Cell` model. Do not create a second IR for region mode.
178: 
179: ### 5.3 Digital PDF validation
180: 
181: The MVP handles digital PDFs with a usable text layer. On import or page selection, detect pages that do not provide usable digital text/position information.
182: 
183: For a page without a usable text layer:
184: 
185: - Do not return an empty table as if extraction succeeded.
186: - Do not silently OCR the viewer image.
187: - Show that the page is image-only or unsupported by the digital MVP.
188: - Keep OCR as a later Part 2 capability.

1032: 
1033: **Non-goals:** several rectangles in one workbook, rectangles spanning pages, automatic merging of results, writing any file other than the `.xlsx`, marking cells in the workbook.
1034: 
1035: ## 2. User flow
1036: 
1037: 1. Import a PDF; the viewer shows a page (page navigation, zoom, pan).
1038: 2. Select the required column order: rightmost PDF column → Excel A (`right_to_left`) or leftmost PDF column → Excel A (`left_to_right`). No default is preselected.
1039: 3. Drag a rectangle; handles allow move and resize. The rectangle is stored in page coordinates.
1040: 4. **Extract:** the app builds the grid for the page, applies the rectangle, and shows (a) a grid preview of the resulting sheet, (b) an alert list, and (c) highlights on the page image for each alerted cell.
1041: 5. **Retry:** the user moves or resizes the rectangle and extracts again.
1042: 6. **Export:** a save dialog (suggested file name; D14) writes one workbook. If alerts remain, a confirmation dialog lists them first.
1043: 
1044: ## 3. Region semantics
1045: 
1046: **Coordinate space.** The rectangle is defined in the page's user space and accounts for page rotation, CropBox/MediaBox offsets and viewer zoom. It is stored with the extraction provenance.
1047: 
1048: **Containment.** A grid cell is *complete* when its full rectangle lies inside the user rectangle within a small tolerance (default 1 pt; tuned in Phase 0). A cell intersecting the boundary is *partial*. A text run whose box crosses the boundary also makes its cell partial.
1049: 
1050: **Grid source.** The full-page grid is reconstructed first (Part 1 §5.9), then intersected with the rectangle. This is what lets the app recognize that a cell continues beyond the selection, instead of silently treating a clipped cell as complete.
1051: 
1052: **Merged and wrapped cells.** Merged cells are reproduced as merged ranges; a merged range crossing the boundary is partial. Wrapped cells are reproduced as displayed (LF at visual line breaks, wrap-text on).
1053: 
1054: **Stacked tables in one rectangle.** Tables are written in vertical order separated by exactly one empty row, and a `multiple-tables` alert is shown so the user can narrow the rectangle (D14).
1055: 
1056: **Ruleless regions.** If the region contains text but no ruling lines, no grid is guessed: the app shows a `ruleless-region` alert and produces no sheet.

29: ///
30: /// Controls how text spans are sorted after extraction from a PDF page.
31: /// The default `TopToBottom` mode uses simple geometric sorting, while
32: /// `ColumnAware` uses the XY-Cut algorithm to detect columns and read
33: /// each column top-to-bottom before moving to the next.
34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
35: pub enum ReadingOrder {
36:     /// Simple top-to-bottom, left-to-right ordering.
37:     ///
38:     /// Sorts spans by Y-coordinate descending (top of page first),
39:     /// then by X-coordinate ascending (left to right).
40:     #[default]
41:     TopToBottom,
42:     /// Column-aware ordering using the XY-Cut algorithm.
43:     ///
44:     /// Detects columns via projection-profile analysis and reads each
45:     /// column fully (top-to-bottom) before moving to the next column.
46:     /// Best for newspapers, academic papers, and multi-column layouts.
47:     ColumnAware,
48:     /// Logical-structure ordering from the document's `/StructTreeRoot`.
49:     ///
50:     /// For a Tagged PDF, ISO 32000-1:2008 §14.8.2.3 makes a pre-order traversal
51:     /// of the structure hierarchy AUTHORITATIVE for reading order - it is the
52:     /// producer's declared sequence, independent of glyph geometry, so it reads
53:     /// tables and complex layouts correctly where a geometric XY-cut guesses.
54:     ///
55:     /// Spans are ordered by their marked-content id (`/MCID`) following that
56:     /// traversal; any span without a matching MCID is appended in geometric
57:     /// (`ColumnAware`) order. When the structure tree is absent or not
58:     /// trustworthy for ordering (untagged, or `/Suspects true`), this falls back
59:     /// to `ColumnAware` entirely, so it is always safe to request.
60:     Structure,
61: }

=== RenderedImage ===

/// A rendered page image.
pub struct RenderedImage {
    /// Raw image data
    pub data: Vec<u8>,
    /// Width in pixels
    pub width: u32,
    /// Height in pixels
    pub height: u32,
    /// Format of the image data
    pub format: ImageFormat,
}

impl RenderedImage {
    /// Save the image to a file.
    pub fn save(&self, path: impl AsRef<std::path::Path>) -> Result<()> {
        std::fs::write(path, &self.data)
            .map_err(|e| Error::InvalidPdf(format!("Failed to write image: {}", e)))
    }

    /// Get the image data as bytes.
    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
        &self.data
    }
}

//! High-level PDF API for simple document creation and manipulation.
//!
//! This module provides a unified, easy-to-use API for common PDF operations:
//! - Creating PDFs from Markdown, HTML, or plain text
//! - Opening and editing existing PDFs with DOM-like navigation
//! - Querying and modifying document content
//! - Converting between formats
//!
//! ## Quick Start - Creating PDFs
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use pdf_oxide::api::Pdf;
//!
//! // Create from Markdown
//! let mut pdf = Pdf::from_markdown("# Hello World\n\nThis is a PDF.")?;
//! pdf.save("output.pdf")?;
//!
//! // Create from HTML
//! let mut pdf = Pdf::from_html("<h1>Hello</h1><p>World</p>")?;
//! pdf.save("output.pdf")?;
//! ```
//!
//! ## Opening and Editing PDFs with DOM Access
//!
//! ```ignore
//! use pdf_oxide::api::Pdf;
//!
//! // Open existing PDF
//! let mut doc = Pdf::open("input.pdf")?;
//!
//! // Get a page for DOM-like navigation
//! let page = doc.page(0)?;
//!
//! // Query elements
//! for text in page.find_text_containing("Hello") {
//!     println!("Found: {} at {:?}", text.text(), text.bbox());
//! }
//!

Implementation:

```rust
pub fn probe_path(path: impl AsRef<Path>, options: ProbeOptions) -> pdf_oxide::Result<DocumentObservation> {
    let mut pdf = Pdf::open(path)?;
    let page_count = pdf.page_count()?;
    let limit = match options.max_pages {
        Some(max) => page_count.min(max),
        None => page_count,
    };
    let mut pages = Vec::with_capacity(limit);
    for index in 0..limit {
        pages.push(probe_page(&mut pdf, index, &options)?);
    }
    Ok(DocumentObservation { page_count, pages })
}
```

`probe_page`:
```rust
fn probe_page(pdf: &mut Pdf, index: usize, options: &ProbeOptions) -> pdf_oxide::Result<PageObservation> {
    let rotation_degrees = pdf.page_rotation(index)?;
    let media_box = pdf.page_media_box(index)?;
    let crop_box = pdf.page_crop_box(index)?;

    let chars = pdf.extract_chars(index)?;
    let spans = pdf.extract_spans(index)?;

    let first_chars = chars.iter().take(options.sample).map(|c| CharObservation {
        ch: c.char,
        bbox: BackendBox::from(c.bbox),
        font_name: c.font_name.clone(),
        font_size: c.font_size,
        origin_x: c.origin_x,
        origin_y: c.origin_y,
        rotation_degrees: c.rotation_degrees,
        advance_width: c.advance_width,
    }).collect();

    let first_spans = spans.iter().take(options.sample).map(|s| SpanObservation {
        text: s.text.clone(),
        bbox: BackendBox::from(s.bbox),
        font_name: s.font_name.clone(),
        font_size: s.font_size,
        sequence: s.sequence,
    }).collect();

    let render = match options.render_dpi {
        Some(dpi) => {
            let opts = RenderOptions {
                dpi,
                format: ImageFormat::RawRgba8,
                ..RenderOptions::default()
            };
            let image = pdf.render_page(index, Some(&opts))?;
            Some(RenderObservation {
                width: image.width,
                height: image.height,
                format: "RawRgba8",
                byte_len: image.data.len(),
            })
        }
        None => None,
    };

    Ok(PageObservation { index, rotation_degrees, media_box, crop_box, char_count: chars.len(), span_count: spans.len(), first_chars, first_spans, render })
}
```

impl RenderOptions {
    /// Set a transparent background (no background fill).
    pub fn with_transparent_background(mut self) -> Self {
        self.background = None;
        self
    }
}

impl RenderOptions {
    /// Create options with specified DPI.
    pub fn with_dpi(dpi: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            dpi,
            ..Default::default()
        }
    }

    /// Set format to JPEG with quality (clamped to 1-100).
    pub fn as_jpeg(mut self, quality: u8) -> Self {
        self.format = ImageFormat::Jpeg;
        self.jpeg_quality = quality.clamp(1, 100);
        self
    }

    /// Set format to raw premultiplied RGBA8888 (no encoding overhead).
    pub fn as_raw(mut self) -> Self {
        self.format = ImageFormat::RawRgba8;
        self
    }
}

+- Identity and source: crates.io `pdf_oxide` 0.3.78; upstream <https://github.com/yfedoseev/pdf_oxide>; documentation <https://pdf.oxide.fyi>. Minimum Rust version declared by the crate: 1.88; the repository toolchain is stable (Rust 1.100.0 at the time of probing).
+- Features probed: crate defaults (`icc`, `legacy-crypto`) plus `rendering`, which pulls `tiny-skia`, `fast_image_resize`, `fontdb`, `harfrust`, `hayro-jbig2` and `hayro-jpeg2000`. The `ocr`, `ml`, `gpu`, `table-ml`, `python`, `parallel`, `signatures` and `fips` features are **not** enabled; OCR is permanently out of scope.
+- Resolved tree: 161 packages with those features, recorded from `cargo tree -p dh-pdf-spike`. Declared licenses across that tree are all permissive (`MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `Zlib`, `0BSD`, `Unlicense`, `CC0-1.0`, `Unicode-3.0`); no GPL, LGPL or AGPL package is declared. This is registry metadata, not a legal audit: `cargo deny` against the exact resolved tree is still required before any adoption.
+- Packaging route: no `-sys` crate and no C system library appears in the probed tree. `fontdb` and `fontconfig-parser` are pure Rust, so this candidate does **not** add Fontconfig linkage of its own (contrast `slint`'s `yeslogic-fontconfig-sys`). That is consistent with the single-executable constraint (D5), but it is a dependency-tree observation, not a measured clean-machine packaging result.
+- Platform evidence: compiles, passes `cargo check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test -p dh-pdf-spike` on Linux. **Windows is not yet verified** for this crate; no CI run exists for the probing branch yet.
+- Reachable API surface, confirmed by compiling the probe: `Pdf::open`, `Pdf::from_bytes`, `page_count`, `page_rotation`, `page_media_box`, `page_crop_box`, `extract_chars`, `extract_spans`, `render_page`.
+- API friction found: `RenderOptions` contains a private field (`scale_override`), so struct-update syntax from outside the crate fails to compile (`E0451`); the supported route is `RenderOptions::with_dpi(dpi).as_raw()`.
+- Explicit-failure behaviour: malformed bytes and a missing path both return `Err` without panicking or reporting an empty document (`malformed_input_is_reported_as_an_error`, `missing_file_is_reported_as_an_error`).
+- **Behavioural evidence is missing and this gate is blocked.** Character/span geometry, font metadata, reading order, page rotation, MediaBox/CropBox values, rendering output, Persian/English/mixed-script handling, and encrypted/corrupt/image-only behaviour have **not** been checked against fixtures. Owner decision A (permitted fixture PDFs and the annotator of expected values) is unanswered, and generating synthetic PDFs as ground truth is prohibited. Windows evidence also needs a CI run.
+- Adoption decision: **none recorded.** Owner decision B (conditional approval to adopt a backend if the spike evidence passes) is unanswered, so there is no decision record and no product crate may use this backend.

```
Stage 2 slice 1 only (repo plan task 2.1: PDF backend prototype and selection).

`crates/dh-pdf-spike` — disposable probe crate, pinned to `pdf_oxide =0.3.78`

decision A has to specify.

  `cargo deny` audit still required.
- No `-sys` crate and no C system library in the tree, so this candidate does
  not add Fontconfig linkage of its own — relevant to D5.
- API friction: `RenderOptions` has a private field, so struct-update syntax
  fails with `E0451`; `RenderOptions::with_dpi(..).as_raw()` is the supported
  route.

C. (needed by slice 3, not this PR) imported-PDF copy-vs-reference policy.
D. Order confirmation that the backend spike precedes viewer work.
```

30: 
31: - Dependency direction: `dh-ir → dh-core/dh-writer → dh-part1 → dh-part2 → dh-part3 → dh-ui/dh-app`. `dh-project` owns private project state plus blank-workbook creation; `dh-xlsx-spike` and `dh-pdf-spike` are isolated Phase 0 evidence, not production dependencies. 35: ## Product constraints (always hold)
36: 
37: - Digital PDF only. Image-only and scanned pages are reported as unsupported; OCR is never invoked, silently or otherwise.
38: - One workbook per project. Each approved capture appends directly below the previous one, with no separator row.

40: - Never overwrite an externally modified workbook.
41: - Excel must be closed before commit or undo. A locked workbook keeps the pending preview and stays retryable.
42: - Private project and capture state lives in the OS application-data directory (`document-harvester/projects.json`). No sidecar file beside the workbook and no hidden state inside the XLSX. Corrupt or missing state fails closed; do not silently overwrite it.

145: 
146: ## 4. Workstream-specific definitions of done
147: 
148: ### W1 — Architecture & Core
149: - Shared types and contracts are explicit and covered by tests.
150: - UI callbacks express intent; application orchestration owns workflow and state transitions.
151: - Private state is versioned and stored in OS application-data.
152: - No dependency direction violates the documented architecture without a recorded reason.
153: - Commit, recovery and undo cannot report success before durable confirmation.
154: 
155: ### W2 — PDF Engineering
156: - Backend identity, version, license and packaging are recorded.
157: - Page metadata and text geometry are independently checked.
158: - Screen/page coordinate transforms pass rotation, crop, zoom and pan tests.
159: - Digital text extraction preserves verified Persian/mixed-script content or reports a precise unsupported case.
160: - Image-only pages are identified; no OCR fallback is silently invoked.
161: 
162: ### W3 — Table Reconstruction
163: - Uses the shared IR and page-level geometry.
164: - Builds page structure before region filtering.
165: - Cell assignment, partial boundaries and unassigned text are testable and visible.
166: - Supports readable cells in ruled and ruleless layouts; uses text geometry and spatial relationships when borders are absent.
167: - Does not silently omit readable text or silently combine separate tables; uncertain content is surfaced as unassigned/ambiguous.
168: - Every preview can be traced to source PDF, page and region.
169: 
170: ### W4 — Excel Engineering
171: - Creates and modifies the project's one workbook.
172: - Appends sequentially with no extra separator row and permits differing table dimensions.
173: - Preserves literal text and safely classifies numeric values.
174: - Uses a tested recoverable write strategy.
175: - Detects workbook mismatch/locks and refuses unsafe operations.
176: - Maintains capture history and only performs undo when safe.
177: 
178: ### W5 — Desktop UI
179: - Main workflow is operable from the desktop UI.
180: - Viewer rectangle remains aligned with page content.
181: - Preview, warnings, approval, retry/cancel, capture history and undo states are clear.
182: - Heavy work is asynchronous and UI remains responsive.
183: - Every visible action has a working outcome or is clearly disabled with an explanation.
184: 
185: ### W6 — QA & Integration
186: - Tests are independent of the implementation wherever ground truth is required.
187: - Unit, integration, failure-injection and end-to-end coverage exists for critical data paths.
188: - Linux and Windows results are recorded.
189: - No silent data loss, duplicate commit, or false success remains in tested failure paths.
190: - Acceptance status is evidence-based; untested is not marked as passed.
191: 
192: ## 5. Integration contracts and handoff rules
193: 
194: | Producer | Must provide | Consumer |
195: |---|---|---|
196: | W1 | Project/session, preview identity, append-plan and capture-record contracts | W2, W3, W4, W5 |
197: | W2 | Page metadata, rendered page, positioned text runs and canonical geometry | W3, W5 |
198: | W3 | Structured preview, source provenance, warnings and approval eligibility | W1, W5 |
199: | W4 | Workbook operations, commit result, lock/integrity errors and undo result | W1, W5 |
200: | W5 | User intents and display projections; no direct XLSX/PDF backend access | W1 |
201: | W6 | Reproducible test fixtures, results, failures and acceptance evidence | All workstreams |
202: 
203: A producer must not ask a consumer to depend on private implementation details. Agree the contract first, add a small fixture/example, then implement against it. Changes to shared contracts require affected workstream owners to review and update tests.
204: 
205: ## 6. Delivery checkpoints
206: 
207: | Checkpoint | Required demonstration | Decision |
208: |---|---|---|
209: | CP0 — Baseline verified | Workspace builds/tests or known failures are recorded; task owners and contracts identified | Start implementation |
210: | CP1 — Project shell | Launch app, create isolated project, create blank workbook, restart safely | Proceed to PDF integration |
211: | CP2 — Viewer selection | Import/display PDF, navigate, zoom/pan, draw rectangle with verified page coordinates | Proceed to extraction |
212: | CP3 — Extraction preview | Digital PDF region becomes structured preview with warnings; no workbook mutation | Proceed to writer integration |
213: | CP4 — First safe append | Approve one preview and append to workbook; failure preserves last valid file | Proceed to sequential captures |
214: | CP5 — Repeated captures and undo | Append different-shaped captures, list history, safe undo latest capture, lock/external-edit refusal | Proceed to hardening |
215: | CP6 — MVP acceptance | Full end-to-end corpus, platform, recovery and packaging evidence | Release candidate decision |
216: 
217: A checkpoint is passed only when its demonstration and evidence exist. A demo alone does not replace automated tests for data-integrity behavior.
218: 
219: ## 7. Project tracking convention
220: 
221: Use one issue/task per task ID in Section 3. Each task should contain:
222: 
223: - Task ID and workstream.
224: - One accountable owner.
225: - Scope and explicit non-goals.
226: - Dependencies (task IDs).
227: - Acceptance criteria and test evidence.
228: - Files/modules expected to change.
229: - Status: `Backlog`, `Ready`, `In Progress`, `Blocked`, `In Review`, or `Done`.
230: - Blocker/decision needed, if any.
231: 
232: **Done** means code is integrated, tests pass, relevant docs are updated, and evidence is linked. A local implementation that has not been integrated or tested is not Done.
233: 
234: Do not invent calendar estimates. After Stage 0, owners may estimate tasks using the repository baseline and chosen dependencies. Re-estimate when a prototype invalidates an assumption.
235: 
236: ## 8. Decisions to raise just in time
237: 
238: The following are not blockers for the initial application shell. Raise each only when the relevant stage needs it, explain options and consequences, and record the owner's decision:
239: 
240: - Project save-dialog timing/naming and source PDF copy-versus-reference policy.
241: - Worksheet naming and column direction.
242: - Partial-cell approval and multiple-table-in-one-rectangle behavior.
243: - Preview cell editing.
244: - Unassigned-text approval gate.
245: - Worksheet RTL/alignment and shared column-width/row-height policy.
246: - Unsupported external workbook feature policy and the exact external-edit comparison definition.
247: - Performance, memory and workbook-size thresholds.
248: - Exact lock behavior on each supported OS.
249: 
250: No default is approved merely because it appears in a task description or prototype.
251:

The Linux build requires Fontconfig development headers, and the runtime must provide Fontconfig. The CI result is compile evidence, not user-desktop visual acceptance.

PDF extraction/rendering verification against fixtures, Farsi/mixed-script verification and Windows evidence remain open.

290: - An independently annotated fixture corpus is required; synthetic fixtures may supplement unit tests but cannot be the sole ground-truth corpus.

20: fn parse(args: &[String]) -> Result<CliOptions, String> {
21:     let mut options = CliOptions::default();
22:     let mut index = 0;
23:     while index < args.len() {
24:         let key = args[index].as_str();
25:         match key {
26:             "--triage-only" => options.triage_only = true,
27:             "--force" => options.force = true,
28:             "--part" | "--input" | "--output" | "--column-order" => {
29:                 index += 1;
30:                 let value = args
31:                     .get(index)
32:                     .ok_or_else(|| format!("missing value for {key}"))?;
33:                 match key {
34:                     "--part" => options.part = Some(value.parse().map_err(|_| "invalid part")?),
35:                     "--input" => options.input = Some(PathBuf::from(value)),
36:                     "--output" => options.output = Some(PathBuf::from(value)),
37:                     "--column-order" => options.column_order = Some(value.clone()),
38:                     _ => unreachable!(),
39:                 }
40:             }
41:             other => return Err(format!("unknown option: {other}")),
42:         }
43:         index += 1;
44:     }
45:     if let Some(part) = options.part {
46:         if !(1..=3).contains(&part) {
47:             return Err("part must be 1, 2 or 3".to_owned());
48:         }
49:     }
50:     Ok(options)
51: }

112: ## 4. Project and workbook lifecycle
113: 
114: ### 4.1 Project model
115: 
116: A project represents one accumulating workbook. It is not one PDF and it is not one selection.
117: 
118: At runtime the application needs a project session containing, at minimum:
119: 
120: - Project identity.
121: - The target workbook path and current saved-file identity/hash.
122: - The active worksheet used for appending.
123: - The current append position.
124: - Imported PDF source records (at least path and content hash for the current session).
125: - The currently selected PDF and page.
126: - The pending selection and preview, if any.
127: - The last successful commit result.
128: 
129: This is a conceptual contract, not a demand to add a new crate. Project orchestration belongs in `dh-app` or a focused module owned by it; region extraction remains in `dh-part3`, and Excel operations remain in `dh-writer`.
130: 
131: ### 4.2 Blank workbook creation
132: 
133: When the user invokes **New Project**, the application must:
134: 
135: 1. Start a new project session; it must not reuse a previous project's in-memory state.
136: 2. Create one valid `.xlsx` workbook with one empty append destination worksheet.
137: 3. Establish the workbook's saved path according to the approved project-save policy.
138: 4. Initialize the append cursor at the first row of the worksheet.
139: 5. Make the project ready for PDF import.
140: 
141: Do not create a template, headings, sample data, hidden review sheet, source labels, or decorative content. The exact worksheet name is not yet owner-confirmed; do not hard-code a product-specific name without recording the decision.
142: 
143: ### 4.3 Project persistence decision
144: 
145: The workbook is the project's primary user-facing output. **Owner decision: private application state is approved.** Persist the project identity, workbook association, committed capture records, append cursor, transaction journal/recovery data, capture history and undo metadata in the operating system's application-data area. This store is separate from the workbook directory: do not create sidecar files beside the workbook, and do not store hidden state or history inside the XLSX. The exact reopen UX and source-PDF copy-versus-reference policy remain open. When a project is reopened, verify the workbook identity/content against the private state before enabling append or undo; stop safely on mismatch.
146: 
147: ### 4.4 Source PDF identity
148: 
149: For each imported PDF, compute a content hash and retain the original path for the session. The hash is used to invalidate cached extraction results when the file changes. If a source file disappears or its content changes, show a clear message; never silently substitute another file with the same name.
150: 
151: Whether PDFs are copied into project storage or referenced in place is pending. The design must isolate this decision behind the source-file management layer.

50: ## Stage S2 — PageTransform and region-selection interface
51: 
52: - `PageTransform` is the single conversion implementation for physical viewport pixels and unrotated PDF page user space. Its `page_box` is the effective CropBox (falling back to MediaBox upstream), and its origin includes viewport placement and pan.
53: - `RegionSelection.rectangle` is a physical-screen-pixel `BBox`; call `RegionSelection::to_page_user_space(&PageTransform)` to obtain the canonical page-space `BBox`.
54: - The conversion validates finite, positive-area input through `PageTransform`, then rejects rectangles extending beyond the effective page box. It does not clip them.
55: - The obsolete `PageGeometry` conversion structure and unimplemented region-operation placeholders were removed from this module; later region operations must be added when their behavior and policy gates are in scope.
56: - Automated region mapping tests cover zoom 1, 2.5 and 4, all quarter-turn rotations, non-zero viewport/pan offsets, and zero-area, NaN and out-of-page rejection. Cross-platform CI is the evidence gate; implementation is not marked complete until it passes.

# Architecture

## Crate boundaries

| Crate | Owns | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `dh-ir` | `TableBlock`, `Cell`, `BBox`, `FontIdentity`, `NumericInfo`, `Provenance`, `GuardStatus`, `CellState`, `TableExtractor` | std only |
| `dh-core` | `JobConfig`, `ColumnOrder`, reason codes, normalization, guard, numeric classification, grid reconstruction, continuation, triage, `JobState`, `state_key`, publish | `dh-ir` |
| `dh-writer` | `XlsxWriter`, `ReviewRow`, worksheet layout, sheet-name/font/overflow policies | `dh-ir`, `dh-core` |
| `dh-part1` | `DigitalExtractor`, validated-font list, batch fast lane, cancellation | `dh-ir`, `dh-core`, `dh-writer` |
| `dh-part2` | `OcrExtractor`, image acquisition, raster detection, backends, merge, calibration, routing, OCR lane | `dh-ir`, `dh-core`, `dh-writer`, `dh-part1` |
| `dh-part3` | region selection, containment, alerts, page cache, single-file export | all above |
| `dh-ui` | plain-data `UiProjection`, `UiBridge`, compiled MVP `MainWindow` and `AboutPanel` | `dh-core`, `slint` |
| `dh-app` | desktop entry point and retained CLI mode | workspace crates, `dh-ui` |


Dependencies point one way only: `ir → core/writer → part1 → part2 → part3 → ui/app`. Core never imports a Part; Parts never import `dh-app`.

## Shared boundaries

- **One IR, one writer.** All three Parts produce `Vec<TableBlock>`; Part 2 populates `raw_confidence` and (only after calibration) `calibrated_confidence`. Part 3 exports through the same writer with `include_review_sheet = false`.
- **Column order is per-job and explicit.** `ColumnOrder` has no `Default` and no implicit value; `from_selection("")` is an error. It is part of `StateKeyInputs` via `JobConfig`.
- **Review artifact.** Batch output has a separate `Review` worksheet (`dh-writer::ReviewRow`); no `.review.csv` and no in-cell markers. Region mode writes only the workbook and keeps alerts in the GUI.
- **Guard is a risk detector.** `dh-core::guard::evaluate` returns `GuardStatus`; it does not make text authoritative. Correctness evidence comes from corpus validation.

## Threading and UI

Manifest Part 1 §6.4 requires core state behind `Arc<Mutex<_>>`, ~10 Hz GUI updates, cooperative cancellation, and no `ModelRc` on worker threads. Workers send plain data and the UI applies it via `Weak::upgrade_in_event_loop`.

`dh-ui::UiProjection` and `UiBridge` remain the plain-data boundary. The MVP desktop shell is now compiled through Slint 1.19.0 from `crates/dh-ui/build.rs`; `dh-app` launches it when no CLI arguments are supplied and retains the existing CLI path when arguments are present.

The compiled UI currently contains the welcome shell and an About panel with the `AboutSlint` attribution widget. The panel is opened from the main window's About button. Slint is used under its Royalty-Free Desktop, Mobile and Web Applications License 2.0; the About panel satisfies the attribution condition. Linux CI installs `libfontconfig1-dev` to build; a Linux runtime must provide Fontconfig. The current CI result proves compilation on Linux and Windows, not a visual/runtime acceptance test on a user's desktop.

The other staged UI views (PDF viewer, selection, preview, history, triage and export) are not yet wired into the MVP shell. The next UI work is the project creation and project workspace flow, followed by the PDF viewer surface.

See [DEPENDENCIES.md](DEPENDENCIES.md) for exact Slint version, features, license and platform notes.
## Deliberately not decided

`StitchMode` has no default (D8), `NumericClassification` keeps conservative text behavior (D13), `ExportGate` is explicit (D14), and confidence thresholds are plain values with no approved target (D11). Do not add defaults that imply owner approval.

```rust
//! Top-level screen navigation for the desktop shell.
//!
//! Task 1.2 (Stage 1) covers navigation and empty states for the project home
//! screen, the project workspace screen and the settings/About placeholder.
//! Screen choice and action availability live here, in the application layer,
//! so they can be tested without a running Slint window. `dh-ui` only renders
//! the resulting state and reports user intent.

/// Which top-level screen the shell is showing.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum Screen {
    /// No project is open: the New Project entry point.
    #[default]
    ProjectHome,
    /// A project is open; its identity and workbook are known.
    ProjectWorkspace,
}

/// Navigation-relevant events reported by the application or the UI.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum NavigationEvent {
    /// Launch found no stored project.
    NoProjectRestored,
    /// A project was created, or a stored project and its workbook were restored.
    ProjectOpened,
    /// A stored project could not be opened because its workbook is missing.
    ProjectWorkbookMissing,
    /// The user asked to start a new project.
    NewProjectRequested,
}

/// Current navigation state.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Navigation {
    screen: Screen,
}

impl Navigation {
    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    pub fn screen(self) -> Screen { self.screen }
    pub fn apply(&mut self, event: NavigationEvent) -> Screen {
        self.screen = match (self.screen, event) {
            (_, NavigationEvent::ProjectOpened) => Screen::ProjectWorkspace,
            (_, NavigationEvent::NewProjectRequested) => Screen::ProjectHome,
            (_, NavigationEvent::ProjectWorkbookMissing) => Screen::ProjectHome,
            (_, NavigationEvent::NoProjectRestored) => Screen::ProjectHome,
        };
        self.screen
    }
    pub fn project_open(self) -> bool { self.screen == Screen::ProjectWorkspace }
}
```

Hmm, the match with all `_` on first element is silly. Simplify:

```rust
pub fn apply(&mut self, event: NavigationEvent) -> Screen {
    self.screen = match event {
        NavigationEvent::ProjectOpened => Screen::ProjectWorkspace,
        NavigationEvent::NoProjectRestored
        | NavigationEvent::ProjectWorkbookMissing
        | NavigationEvent::NewProjectRequested => Screen::ProjectHome,
    };
    self.screen
}
```

That's a pure function of event; `Navigation` wrapper holds state. Fine and honest.

But then `NoProjectRestored` etc. are redundant. Still useful as named events. Keep.

```rust
/// A user action the shell can expose.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Action {
    ChooseParentDirectory,
    CreateProject,
    NewProject,
    ImportPdf,
    OpenAbout,
}

/// Whether an action is usable, hidden, or visible but disabled.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Availability {
    /// The action works on this screen.
    Enabled,
    /// Visible but disabled; the shell shows this explanation next to it.
    Disabled(&'static str),
    /// Not part of this screen.
    Hidden,
}

/// Explanation shown for controls whose feature does not exist yet.
pub const NOT_AVAILABLE_YET: &str = "PDF import is not available yet.";

/// Minimum data needed to decide whether project creation can proceed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ProjectForm {
    pub name_present: bool,
    pub parent_directory_present: bool,
    pub busy: bool,
}

impl ProjectForm {
    pub fn for_values(name: &str, parent_directory: &str, busy: bool) -> Self {
        Self {
            name_present: !name.trim().is_empty(),
            parent_directory_present: !parent_directory.trim().is_empty(),
            busy,
        }
    }
}

/// Availability of `action` on `screen` given the current form contents.
pub fn availability(screen: Screen, action: Action, form: ProjectForm) -> Availability {
    match (screen, action) {
        (Screen::ProjectHome, Action::ChooseParentDirectory) => Availability::Enabled,
        (Screen::ProjectHome, Action::CreateProject) => {
            if form.busy {
                Availability::Disabled("A project is being created.")
            } else if !form.name_present {
                Availability::Disabled("Enter a project name.")
            } else if !form.parent_directory_present {
                Availability::Disabled("Choose where the project folder will be created.")
            } else {
                Availability::Enabled
            }
        }
        (Screen::ProjectWorkspace, Action::NewProject) => Availability::Enabled,
        (_, Action::OpenAbout) => Availability::Enabled,
        (_, Action::ImportPdf) => Availability::Disabled(NOT_AVAILABLE_YET),
        _ => Availability::Hidden,
    }
}
```

```rust
pub enum Screen { ProjectHome, ProjectWorkspace }
pub enum NavigationEvent { NoProjectRestored, ProjectOpened, ProjectWorkbookMissing, NewProjectRequested }
pub struct Navigation { screen: Screen }
pub enum Action { CreateProject, ImportPdf }
pub enum Availability { Enabled, Disabled(&'static str), Hidden }
```

For CreateProject:
```rust
pub fn availability(screen: Screen, action: Action, form: ProjectForm) -> Availability {
    match (screen, action) {
        (Screen::ProjectHome, Action::CreateProject) => {
            if form.busy {
                Availability::Disabled("A project is being created.")
            } else if !form.name_present {
                Availability::Disabled("Enter a project name.")
            } else if !form.parent_directory_present {
                Availability::Disabled("Choose where the project folder will be created.")
            } else {
                Availability::Enabled
            }
        }
        (Screen::ProjectWorkspace, Action::CreateProject) => Availability::Hidden,
        (Screen::ProjectWorkspace, Action::ImportPdf) => Availability::Disabled(NOT_AVAILABLE_YET),
        (Screen::ProjectHome, Action::ImportPdf) => Availability::Hidden,
    }
}
```

In dh-app:
```rust
fn refresh_create_project(window: &dh_ui::MainWindow, name: &str, directory: &str, busy: bool) {
    let availability = navigation::availability(
        Screen::ProjectHome,
        Action::CreateProject,
        ProjectForm::for_values(name, directory, busy),
    );
    match availability {
        Availability::Enabled => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(true);
            window.set_create_project_note("".into());
        }
        Availability::Disabled(reason) => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(false);
            window.set_create_project_note(reason.into());
        }
        Availability::Hidden => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(false);
            window.set_create_project_note("".into());
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// Push the navigation state into the shell.
fn apply_screen(window: &dh_ui::MainWindow, navigation: Navigation) {
    window.set_project_open(navigation.project_open());
    window.set_empty_state_message(empty_state_message(navigation.screen()).into());
}

/// Push the Create Project availability and its explanation into the shell.
fn refresh_create_project(
    window: &dh_ui::MainWindow,
    name: &str,
    parent_directory: &str,
    busy: bool,
) {
    match availability(
        Screen::ProjectHome,
        Action::CreateProject,
        ProjectForm::for_values(name, parent_directory, busy),
    ) {
        Availability::Enabled => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(true);
            window.set_create_project_note("".into());
        }
        Availability::Disabled(reason) => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(false);
            window.set_create_project_note(reason.into());
        }
        Availability::Hidden => {
            window.set_create_project_enabled(false);
            window.set_create_project_note("".into());
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
fn run_desktop_application() {
    let store = match dh_project::ProjectStore::from_os_app_data() {
        Ok(store) => store,
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("cannot initialize private application data: {error}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    let window = match dh_ui::new_main_window() {
        Ok(window) => window,
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("failed to create Document Harvester window: {error}");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    };

    // PDF import is the Stage 2 workflow and does not exist yet; report it as
    // a disabled control with an explanation rather than a dead button.
    window.set_import_pdf_enabled(false);
    window.set_import_pdf_note(NOT_AVAILABLE_YET.into());

    let mut navigation = Navigation::new();
    match store.current_project() {
        Err(error) => {
            navigation.apply(NavigationEvent::ProjectNotOpened);
            window.set_status_message(
                format!("Private project state could not be read: {error}").into(),
            );
        }
        Ok(Some(project)) if project.workbook_path.is_file() => {
            navigation.apply(NavigationEvent::ProjectOpened);
            window.set_project_name(project.name.clone().into());
            window.set_parent_directory(
                project
                    .project_directory
                    .parent()
                    .unwrap_or(&project.project_directory)
                    .to_string_lossy()
                    .to_string()
                    .into(),
            );
            window.set_workbook_path(project.workbook_path.to_string_lossy().to_string().into());
            window.set_status_message("Last project restored from private application data.".into());
        }
        Ok(Some(_)) => {
            navigation.apply(NavigationEvent::ProjectNotOpened);
            window.set_status_message(
                "The last project's workbook is missing. Create a new project.".into(),
            );
        }
        Ok(None) => {
            navigation.apply(NavigationEvent::NoProjectStored);
        }
    }
    apply_screen(&window, navigation);
    refresh_create_project(
        &window,
        &window.get_project_name(),
        &window.get_parent_directory(),
        false,
    );
```

Content:
```markdown
## Stage S1 — project home and workspace navigation

- `dh-app/src/navigation.rs` owns the shell's screen model: `Screen::ProjectHome` when no project is open, `Screen::ProjectWorkspace` when one is. `Navigation::apply` maps `NavigationEvent::{NoProjectStored, ProjectOpened, ProjectNotOpened, NewProjectRequested}` to a screen; the resulting screen is fixed by the event, so every copy of the state agrees.
- `availability(screen, action, form)` decides whether a control works, is hidden, or is visible but disabled with the text to show. `Action::CreateProject` is enabled only on project home with a non-blank name and a chosen folder and while no creation is running; `Action::ImportPdf` is disabled on the workspace with `NOT_AVAILABLE_YET` ("PDF import is not available yet.") because Stage 2 owns PDF import.
- `empty_state_message(Screen::ProjectWorkspace)` returns `EMPTY_PROJECT_MESSAGE` ("No captures yet."). No capture or append path exists yet, so this is a constant; Stage 5 must replace it with real capture state.
- `MainWindow.slint` exposes `project-open`, `empty-state-message`, `create-project-enabled`, `create-project-note`, `import-pdf-enabled` and `import-pdf-note` as properties plus the `project-form-changed(string, string)` callback. It renders and reports intent only; it holds no screen logic.
- The About panel (`AboutPanel` with `AboutSlint`) is unchanged and is reachable from both screens. No Settings screen exists: OCR settings belong to Part 2 and blueprint §8.3 keeps those views out of the digital MVP navigation.
- `dh-ui/build.rs` compiles only `ui/MainWindow.slint`; `RegionView`, `BatchView`, `OcrSettingsView`, `ReviewView`, `TriageView`, `ExportDialog` and `ColumnOrderDialog` are still unstaged, uncompiled scaffold files and are not reachable from the shell.
```

50: ## Stage S2 — PageTransform and region-selection interface
51: 
52: - `PageTransform` is the single conversion implementation for physical viewport pixels and unrotated PDF page user space. Its `page_box` is the effective CropBox (falling back to MediaBox upstream), and its origin includes viewport placement and pan.
53: - `RegionSelection.rectangle` is a physical-screen-pixel `BBox`; call `RegionSelection::to_page_user_space(&PageTransform)` to obtain the canonical page-space `BBox`.
54: - The conversion validates finite, positive-area input through `PageTransform`, then rejects rectangles extending beyond the effective page box. It does not clip them.
55: - The obsolete `PageGeometry` conversion structure and unimplemented region-operation placeholders were removed from this module; later region operations must be added when their behavior and policy gates are in scope.
56: - Automated region mapping tests cover zoom 1, 2.5 and 4, all quarter-turn rotations, non-zero viewport/pan offsets, and zero-area, NaN and out-of-page rejection. Cross-platform CI is the evidence gate; implementation is not marked complete until it passes.

A full live workbook preview is useful but was not explicitly confirmed as mandatory. The minimum required display is the preview of the pending selection and clear confirmation of where it will be appended.

### 8.2 UI state and callbacks

Keep the current plain-data boundary in `dh-ui/src/lib.rs` (`UiProjection`, `UiBridge`, `SharedUiState`). Extend the projection for project status, PDF/page information, selection geometry, extraction preview, append destination and commit result.

Callbacks should express user intent only, for example:

- `new_project`.
- `import_pdf`.
- `select_pdf`.
- `previous_page` / `next_page`.
- `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` / `pan`.
- `selection_changed`.
- `extract_region`.
- `retry_region`.
- `approve_selection`.
- `cancel_preview`.

The callbacks should dispatch commands to the application layer. They should not contain PDF parser calls, table reconstruction logic, or workbook-writing logic.

### 8.3 Current UI scaffold gap

The desktop shell and New Project/project-workbook lifecycle are implemented. The PDF region workflow remains a scaffold: no PDF rendering widget, PDF import, page navigation, pointer-driven rectangle geometry, digital extraction, preview or commit-to-workbook flow is implemented yet. Treat the Region workflow as the next major UI path; keep OCR out of the digital-only MVP.

For the MVP, the Region workflow should become the primary application path. The batch/OCR screens can remain staged or hidden from the primary MVP navigation; do not spend implementation effort completing Part 2 screens for this release.

### 8.4 Threading

Follow the existing architecture's Slint threading rules:

- Parsing and extraction run off the UI thread.
- The UI receives plain Rust data and updates the projection on the UI thread.
- Do not pass Slint `ModelRc` objects to worker threads.
- Throttle progress/long-operation UI updates where relevant.
- Disable conflicting actions while a selection is extracting or committing.

## 9. Repository change map

The paths below identify the likely files to extend. New module names are suggestions for organization, not proof that files already exist.

| Path | Planned work | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/dh-ir/src/lib.rs` | Review `TableBlock`, `Cell`, `BBox`, `Provenance` and `CellState::Partial`; add only missing, justified source/selection metadata while preserving the shared IR | High |
| `crates/dh-core/src/config.rs` | Define the MVP's explicit project/selection configuration boundary; resolve how existing `ColumnOrder` is selected and scoped | High |
| `crates/dh-core/src/reason.rs` | Reuse existing reason codes; add a code only when a real, distinct condition needs one | High |

| 4 | Create Project enablement lived in Slint (`name != "" && dir != ""`), no explanation when disabled, no re-check on edit | Yes |
| 5 | `create-another-project` reset state ad hoc; `project-created` was a second copy of "is a project open" | Yes |
| 6 | About existed as a floating panel only | Partially — About already worked; reachable from both screens now |

=== scaffold section ===
## Stage S1 — project home and workspace navigation

- `dh_app::navigation` owns the shell's screen model. `Screen::ProjectHome` is shown when no project is open; `Screen::ProjectWorkspace` when one is. `NavigationEvent` names the causes (`NoProjectStored`, `ProjectOpened`, `ProjectNotOpened`, `NewProjectRequested`) and each event fixes the resulting screen, so the decision is testable without a Slint window.
- `MainWindow.slint` no longer has a `create-another-project` callback. It reports `new-project()` instead, and the returned-from-workspace state is the same project home the launch path uses. The `project-created` bool was replaced by `project-open`, which is derived from the screen rather than tracked separately.
- Control availability is decided in `navigation::availability`, not in Slint. `CreateProject` is enabled only with a non-blank name and parent folder and while not busy; each disabled case carries its own one-line explanation. `ImportPdf` is `Disabled("PDF import is not available yet.")` in the workspace and hidden on project home — it is not wired to any backend.
- The workspace empty state is the constant `EMPTY_PROJECT_MESSAGE` ("No captures yet.") because no capture or append path exists yet. Stage 5, which owns append and capture history, must replace the constant with real capture state instead of extending it.
- No Settings screen was added. The only documented settings are the Part 2 OCR backend, languages, DPI and thresholds, which blueprint §8.3 keeps out of the digital-only MVP shell; adding one would invent an undocumented flow. The About panel is unchanged, still contains `AboutSlint`, and is reachable from both screens.
- Automated evidence is the `dh-app::navigation` unit tests (screen transitions in both directions, launch/restore/cannot-open, each Create Project disabled reason, the disabled PDF-import note, and the empty-state ownership). The compiled `.slint` layout has no unit-test oracle; its evidence is the CI compile plus the owner's visual check listed in the Stage 1 owner test.

   - Add characterization tests for: strings beginning with =, +, -, @ stored and read back as text (never as formulas); text near and over the 32,767-character cell limit; rows and columns at and beyond Excel's 1,048,576 x 16,384 limits; large integers and floats beyond 15 significant digits; leading-zero identifiers; and round-trip behavior for features a user might add in a spreadsheet app (charts, images, conditional formatting, data validation, defined names, comments, hyperlinks, freeze panes, column widths, sheet protection, Excel tables).
   - These are characterization tests: record what the backend actually does (kept, altered, dropped, error). Do not assert a policy and do not decide what the product should do about dropped features. That decision is deferred (plan Section 8).

This document records the current execution state; it distinguishes completed evidence from provisional choices and unstarted production work.

**Merged implementation baseline (`main`, PR #1):**
- Repository baseline inspection confirmed the existing Rust/Slint scaffold and its current stubs.

- Added the isolated `dh-xlsx-spike` crate; its four tests pass on Linux and Windows. Evidence: [CI run 44912824313](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester/actions/runs/44912824313), commit `ebc9647`.

- `dh-app` now launches the Slint shell when no CLI arguments are supplied and retains the prior CLI mode when arguments are supplied.

**Technical choices and gates:**
- Slint 1.19.0 is integrated under its Royalty-Free desktop license; the About panel contains the required `AboutSlint` attribution. The Linux build requires Fontconfig development headers, and the runtime must provide Fontconfig. The CI result is compile evidence, not user-desktop visual acceptance.
- `umya-spreadsheet = 3.1.1` is integrated provisionally in the production path through `dh-writer` and `dh-project`; it is not merely isolated in `dh-xlsx-spike`. Full transitive dependency/license audit and Stage 5 integrity/fidelity tests remain open.
- `calamine = 0.38.0` is used only as an independent reader in spike tests.
- No PDF dependency is selected or adopted. The isolated `dh-pdf-spike` crate records the `pdf_oxide 0.3.78` dependency register and reachable API surface only (Stage 2 task 2.1, gate blocked). PDF extraction/rendering verification against fixtures, Farsi/mixed-script verification and Windows evidence remain open.

**Next implementation target:** finish user-visible New Project/workbook acceptance; acquire and independently annotate real digital-PDF/reference-workbook fixtures; then prototype PDF rendering, text geometry and coordinate mapping without selecting a PDF engine before evidence.

**In review — Stage 1 task 1.2 (project home and workspace navigation):**
- `dh-app::navigation` now owns the two-screen model, the Create Project availability rules and the empty-project state; `MainWindow.slint` renders project home, the project workspace and the unchanged About panel. PDF import is visible but disabled with "PDF import is not available yet."; no viewer, selection, preview, append, history or undo control was added or faked.
- No Settings screen was added: the only documented settings are Part 2 OCR options, which blueprint §8.3 keeps out of the digital-only MVP. This is recorded in [SCAFFOLD.md](SCAFFOLD.md#stage-s1--project-home-and-workspace-navigation).
- Automated evidence is the `dh-app::navigation` unit tests named in the 1.2 row. The `.slint` layout itself has no unit-test oracle; CI compile plus owner visual check is the remaining evidence. CI evidence recorded: [run 45001695632](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester/actions/runs/45001695632) (PR #8 head `dad1794`, Ubuntu and Windows both success); owner visual acceptance remains pending.

Other status and constraints:
- PR #1 is closed and merged into `main` at `ca13f60d300e69b4c3ace03a3b2cacbd667a745f`: [PR #1](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester/pull/1).
- New Project and blank-workbook creation are implemented. PDF import, page rendering, region selection, digital text extraction, preview and approved-capture append are not yet implemented.

41: - Features probed: crate defaults (`icc`, `legacy-crypto`) plus `rendering`, which pulls `tiny-skia`, `fast_image_resize`, `fontdb`, `harfrust`, `hayro-jbig2` and `hayro-jpeg2000`. The `ocr`, `ml`, `gpu`, `table-ml`, `python`, `parallel`, `signatures` and `fips` features are **not** enabled; OCR is permanently out of scope.
42: - Resolved tree: 161 packages including the probe crate, recorded from `cargo tree -p dh-pdf-spike`. Adding the probe to the workspace lockfile added 30 packages and changed **no existing package version**. Declared licenses across that tree are all permissive (`MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `Zlib`, `0BSD`, `Unlicense`, `CC0-1.0`, `Unicode-3.0`); no GPL, LGPL or AGPL package is declared. Where the workspace already used an older minor of the same crate (`harfrust`, `skrifa`, `read-fonts`, `write-fonts`, `nom`, `roxmltree`, `weezl`, `jiff`, `taffy`), the lockfile now carries both versions rather than upgrading the existing one. This is registry metadata, not a legal audit: `cargo deny` against the exact resolved tree is still required before any adoption.
43: - Packaging route: no `-sys` crate and no C system library appears in the probed tree. `fontdb` and `fontconfig-parser` are pure Rust, so this candidate does **not** add Fontconfig linkage of its own (contrast `slint`'s `yeslogic-fontconfig-sys`). That is consistent with the single-executable constraint (D5), but it is a dependency-tree observation, not a measured clean-machine packaging result.
44: - Platform evidence: compiles, passes `cargo check`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo test -p dh-pdf-spike` on Linux. **Windows is not yet verified** for this crate; no CI run exists for the probing branch yet.
45: - Reachable API surface, confirmed by compiling the probe: `Pdf::open`, `Pdf::from_bytes`, `page_count`, `page_rotation`, `page_media_box`, `page_crop_box`, `extract_chars`, `extract_spans`, `render_page`.
46: - API friction found: `RenderOptions` contains a private field (`scale_override`), so struct-update syntax from outside the crate fails to compile (`E0451`); the supported route is `RenderOptions::with_dpi(dpi).as_raw()`.
47: - Explicit-failure behaviour: malformed bytes and a missing path both return `Err` without panicking or reporting an empty document (`malformed_input_is_reported_as_an_error`, `missing_file_is_reported_as_an_error`).
48: - **Behavioural evidence is missing and this gate is blocked.** Character/span geometry, font metadata, reading order, page rotation, MediaBox/CropBox values, rendering output, Persian/English/mixed-script handling, and encrypted/corrupt/image-only behaviour have **not** been checked against fixtures. Owner decision A (permitted fixture PDFs and the annotator of expected values) is unanswered, and generating synthetic PDFs as ground truth is prohibited. Windows evidence also needs a CI run.
49: - Adoption decision: **none recorded.** Owner decision B (conditional approval to adopt a backend if the spike evidence passes) is unanswered, so there is no decision record and no product crate may use this backend.

1: # Document Harvester — MVP Phase 0 Technical Findings
2: 
3: **Document ID:** DH-MVP-P0-001  
4: **Version:** 0.2 — Preliminary research plus initial XLSX prototype evidence  
5: **Date:** 21 November 2026  
6: **Scope:** Digital PDF region capture and repeated append into one project XLSX workbook  
7: **Repository:** [SMozaff/Document-Harvester](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester)
8: 
9: > **Status:** PDF candidate evaluation remains desk research only. The XLSX candidate has passed an initial, bounded prototype on Linux and Windows, but it is only provisionally selected for the first project/workbook lifecycle slice. No production dependency is approved; full dependency/license audit, spreadsheet-application inspection, and remaining integrity tests are still open.
10: 
11: ## 1. Executive finding
12: 
13: Two candidates deserve first-round prototypes:
14: 
15: 1. **PDF extraction and possible rendering: `pdf_oxide`** — its documentation describes character-level text with bounding boxes and font metadata, reading-order strategies, RTL support claims, page geometry, and an optional pure-Rust renderer.
16: 2. **XLSX read/modify/write: `umya-spreadsheet`** — its documentation describes reading existing XLSX files, changing cell values and styles, and writing the workbook back.
17: 
18: These candidates address the two largest MVP feasibility risks. The XLSX candidate now has initial reproducible evidence; the PDF candidate has not yet been prototyped. Continue to base decisions on generated workbook fixtures and representative project PDFs, not benchmark claims or feature lists alone.
19: 
20: ## 2. PDF extraction and rendering candidate
21: 
22: ### 2.1 `pdf_oxide`
23: 
24: Public documentation reviewed:
25: 
26: - Crate: [pdf_oxide on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/pdf_oxide/latest)
27: - Rust API: [Rust API reference](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/reference/rust-api)
28: - Text extraction: [Text extraction documentation](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/extraction/text)
29: - Rendering: [Page rendering documentation](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/extraction/rendering)
30: - Page geometry: [Page operations](https://pdf.oxide.fyi/rust/docs/editing/pages)
31: 
32: What the documentation claims:
33: 
34: - Latest stable crate shown by docs.rs during this review: `0.3.78`.
35: - License: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (dual license), according to the crate documentation.
36: - Rust-native API; the Rust crate is described as the source of truth.
37: - Text extraction levels include full page, spans and individual characters.
38: - Character/span results can include bounding boxes and font metadata.
39: - Character results can include origin, advance width, rotation and transformation matrix.
40: - The documentation describes multiple reading-order strategies and support for RTL scripts, including Arabic and Hebrew.
41: - Page rotation, MediaBox and CropBox information are exposed.
42: - Optional `rendering` feature provides a pure-Rust renderer using tiny-skia, fontdb and rustybuzz; documentation says it does not require Poppler or MuPDF.
43: - Renderer documentation describes raw RGBA output, which may be suitable for conversion into the image representation used by the Slint viewer.
44: 
45: Why it is relevant:
46: 
47: - Character-level geometry is more useful for table reconstruction and boundary checks than plain extracted text.
48: - Font metadata can feed the existing `FontIdentity` model.
49: - Rotation and page-box APIs may reduce the amount of custom PDF geometry parsing.
50: - A pure-Rust renderer may simplify deployment compared with shipping a separate PDFium runtime.
51: 
52: Important limitations and unknowns:
53: 
54: - The documentation's RTL support statement is not proof of correct Persian extraction in this project's PDFs. Test Persian, Arabic, mixed-script and embedded-font documents separately.
55: - A span's font name/size is not necessarily enough to reconstruct the exact PDF font identity, encoding, ToUnicode map and CID evidence required by the existing IR. Prototype the exact fields available.
56: - Reading order can be logical, visual, content-stream order or geometry-derived. The adapter must preserve raw run order and record evidence rather than silently assuming one order.
57: - Renderer font fallback may use fonts installed on the host. This must be tested on clean Linux and Windows systems, including missing-font behavior and Farsi glyph shaping.
58: - The optional rendering feature adds dependencies and must be included in the license/deployment inventory.
59: - Public benchmark results are vendor-maintained and must not be treated as acceptance evidence for our corpus.
60: 
61: **Preliminary assessment:** Strong first prototype candidate for both digital text extraction and page rendering. Not approved until the API and Farsi corpus tests pass.
62: 
63: ## 3. XLSX read/modify/write candidate
64: 
65: ### 3.1 `umya-spreadsheet`
66: 
67: Public documentation reviewed:
68: 
69: - Crate: [umya-spreadsheet on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/crate/umya-spreadsheet/latest)
70: - API documentation: [umya-spreadsheet API](https://docs.rs/umya-spreadsheet/latest/umya_spreadsheet/)
71: - Repository: [MathNya/umya-spreadsheet](https://github.com/MathNya/umya-spreadsheet)
72: 
73: What the documentation claims:
74: 
75: - Latest stable release shown during this review: `3.1.1` (2026-10-12). A `4.0.0-beta.1` is also listed; do not use the beta as the default candidate.
76: - License: MIT, according to docs.rs and the project README.
77: - Pure-Rust library for reading and writing XLSX files.
78: - Supports opening an existing workbook, editing cell values/styles, and writing it.
79: - Supports creating a new workbook.
80: - Documents worksheet, cell, style, row/column, chart, drawing and image operations; some advanced areas are marked as inconvenient or incompletely documented.
81: - Provides a lazy reader for large workbooks.
82: 
83: Why it is relevant:
84: 
85: - Unlike a write-only XLSX generator, it has a documented read/modify/write workflow.
86: - It appears capable of creating the blank workbook once and modifying the same workbook after each approved selection.
87: - It supports styles and merged-cell-related workbook structures; actual round-trip fidelity still needs testing.
88: 
89: Important limitations and unknowns:
90: 
91: - The docs.rs package listing shows a substantial source package and a non-trivial dependency tree. Record the full resolved dependency/license inventory using `cargo tree` and `cargo deny` before adoption.
92: - The library's reader may load substantial workbook state into memory. Benchmark repeated appends at realistic project sizes.
93: - Public support tables do not guarantee perfect round-trip preservation of every Excel feature. The MVP creates its own simple workbook, which reduces but does not remove this risk.
94: - The initial prototype has verified blank creation, repeated reopen/append, independent read-back, Persian/mixed-script and ZWNJ text, numeric values, and retention of a formula, cell style and merged range across another append.
95: - The initial prototype also verified that a failed write to a separate temporary path does not change the bytes of the last committed workbook.
96: - These tests do not establish arbitrary Excel feature preservation, external-edit detection, workbook lock behavior, undo safety, crash recovery, or realistic resource limits.
97: - Pin an exact stable version; do not use a floating dependency or the 4.0 beta without a separate review.
98: 
99: **Preliminary assessment:** `umya-spreadsheet = 3.1.1` is provisionally selected for Stage 1 blank-workbook creation and the initial project lifecycle. It remains a candidate, not an approved production dependency, until the full dependency/license audit and remaining Stage 5 integrity/fidelity tests pass.
100: 
101: ### 3.2 Why `rust_xlsxwriter` alone is not sufficient
102: 
103: The official crate documentation says `rust_xlsxwriter` writes new XLSX files and cannot modify an existing file. It remains useful for creating new files, but cannot alone implement the straightforward repeated-append workflow.
104: 
105: Reference: [rust_xlsxwriter docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rust_xlsxwriter/latest/rust_xlsxwriter/).
106:

124: ## 5. Phase 0 prototype plan
125: 
126: ### Prototype A — PDF engine
127: 
128: Build a disposable spike (not production integration) that:
129: 
130: 1. Opens a representative PDF and enumerates pages.
131: 2. Reads page rotation, MediaBox and CropBox.
132: 3. Extracts individual characters and spans from at least one page.
133: 4. Records each character's Unicode value, bounding box, origin, advance, rotation, font name and other available metadata.
134: 5. Compares extracted order with the actual visual reading order for Persian, English and mixed-script lines.
135: 6. Renders the same page using the optional renderer.
136: 7. Converts a known rectangle between PDF page coordinates and rendered image coordinates.
137: 8. Repeats for rotated pages, non-zero page boxes, zoom levels and pan offsets.
138: 9. Runs on clean Linux and Windows packaging targets.
139: 10. Records unsupported, missing-font, malformed-file and image-only-page behavior.
140: 
141: Required sample classes:
142: 
143: - Farsi-only text with embedded fonts.
144: - Farsi and English in the same cell.
145: - Arabic-Indic, Persian and Latin digits.
146: - Table with ruled grid lines.
147: - Table without visible ruling.
148: - Merged cells.
149: - Wrapped text / multi-line cells.
150: - Rotated page.
151: - Non-zero CropBox offset.
152: - Text that touches or crosses a proposed selection boundary.
153: - Image-only page to confirm that the digital MVP reports it as unsupported.
154: 
155: ### Prototype B — workbook backend
156: 
157: Build a disposable spike that:
158: 
159: 1. Creates one blank workbook.
160: 2. Writes a first table.
161: 3. Appends a second table directly below it, with a different number of columns.
162: 4. Preserves intentional blank cells and internal blank rows.
163: 5. Writes Persian, English, mixed-script text, numeric values and text identifiers with leading zeroes.
164: 6. Writes a merged range and shifts a second merged range by the correct row offset.
165: 7. Saves, closes and reopens the workbook.
166: 8. Appends a third table after reopening.
167: 9. Opens the result with an independent XLSX reader and checks values, types, ranges and merged-cell definitions.
168: 10. Simulates a failed write and verifies that the last valid workbook is preserved.
169: 11. Benchmarks memory and runtime at realistic workbook sizes.
170: 12. Runs on Linux and Windows.
171: 
172: ### Prototype B — initial executed evidence (21 November 2026)
173: 
174: The disposable spike now lives in `crates/dh-xlsx-spike`. It is an isolated workspace test crate; neither candidate is a dependency of `dh-writer` or any production crate.
175: 
176: **Pinned prototype dependencies:**
177: - Writer/read candidate: `umya-spreadsheet = 3.1.1` (MIT).
178: - Independent XLSX reader: `calamine = 0.38.0` (MIT), used only as a development dependency in the spike.
179: 
180: **Executed test coverage:**
181: 1. Create a blank workbook and verify its default worksheet using the independent reader.
182: 2. Reopen the same workbook, append one capture, reopen again and append a second capture directly below the first.
183: 3. Verify differing capture widths, no inserted separator row, Persian text, English/Persian mixed text, ZWNJ, and a numeric cell using the independent reader.
184: 4. Create a formula, cell style and merged range; reopen, append, save and verify those features remain. Verify the formula separately with the independent reader.
185: 5. Attempt a failed write to a temporary path whose parent directory does not exist; verify the committed workbook's original bytes remain unchanged.
186: 
187: **Observed result:** All four spike tests passed on both `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`, with `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`. Evidence: [GitHub Actions run 20](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester/actions/runs/44912824313), commit `ebc9647`.
188: 
189: **Limits of this result:** This is not an Excel or LibreOffice open/repair test. It does not prove preservation of charts, drawings, row heights, column widths, workbook metadata, external edits or unsupported Excel features. It does not test Excel lock behavior, undo, crash recovery, atomic replacement, performance or memory at realistic workbook sizes. Those remain explicit gates. The temporary-write test validates the candidate's failure behavior for a separate temp path; production transaction/replace logic still requires its own tests.
190: 
191: ### Prototype C — Slint image surface
192: 
193: The MVP desktop shell now compiles with Slint 1.19.0 on Linux and Windows. It uses the Winit backend and software renderer, and the About panel includes the `AboutSlint` attribution widget under the Royalty-Free desktop license. Evidence: [CI run 44914052466](https://github.com/SMozaff/Document-Harvester/actions/runs/44914052466), commit `26b0a14`.
194: 
195: This does **not** prove the UI launches or renders correctly on a user's desktop. The image-surface, PDF page rendering, pointer rectangle overlay, zoom/pan anchoring and page-coordinate mapping are still unimplemented.
196: 
197: Prototype the minimum image surface:
198: 
199: - Pass a rendered page image to Slint.
200: - Display it at fit-to-window and fixed zoom.
201: - Draw a pointer-driven rectangle overlay.
202: - Convert the overlay into page coordinates.
203: - Verify that the rectangle remains anchored to the same PDF content during zoom and pan.
204: 
205: Do not build the full UI before the coordinate and image pipeline is proven.

207: ## 6. Repository observations that affect the plan
208:

262: 
263: ## 10. Review-driven feasibility and integrity tests
264: 
265: The owner has confirmed three product decisions that shape the Phase 0 design:
266: 
267: 1. Private persistent state is approved in the operating system's application-data area, separate from the workbook directory. No sidecar files may be created beside the workbook, and no hidden application state may be written into the XLSX.
268: 2. Excel must be closed before commit or undo. If the workbook is locked, the pending preview must remain available for retry.
269: 3. Both a capture history list and undo of the most recent committed capture are required. Undo must be refused if external workbook modification or any other condition makes rollback unsafe.
270: 
271: These are requirements, not evidence that an implementation already exists. Add the following to the disposable prototypes:
272: 
273: ### 10.1 Private state and crash recovery
274: 
275: - Persist project/workbook association, append cursor, stable capture IDs, committed capture records, transaction journal, and undo metadata in OS application-data storage.
276: - Simulate termination before temporary write, during temporary write, after replacement and before journal finalization.
277: - On restart, reconcile the workbook and journal without duplicate appends or overwriting externally modified data.
278: - Test missing, corrupt, stale and mismatched private state.
279: - Confirm no state files are created in the workbook directory and no hidden worksheet or metadata is added to the XLSX.
280: 
281: ### 10.2 Excel lock, external edits and undo
282: 
283: - On Windows, test the workbook while open in Excel; on Linux, test relevant file locks and replacement semantics.
284: - Confirm a locked workbook leaves the preview pending and retry succeeds after the workbook is closed.
285: - Modify cells and workbook structure externally between appends; confirm the app detects the mismatch and refuses append/recovery/undo rather than silently losing edits.
286: - Test latest-capture undo after multiple appends, application restart and a clean reopen.
287: - Confirm undo refuses after external edits and cannot remove unrelated content.
288: - Test charts, formulas, styles, merged ranges, row heights and column widths through read/modify/write and independent-reader verification. Do not claim arbitrary Excel feature preservation unless demonstrated.
289: 
290: ### 10.3 Text accounting and XLSX cell safety
291: 
292: - Detect text runs inside the selected rectangle that are not assigned to a reconstructed cell; surface an `unassigned-text` warning with source-page coordinates.
293: - Verify formula-like strings (for example `=A1` and `+SUM(A1:A2)`) are written as literal text, not formulas.
294: - Verify ambiguous strings such as `00125`, `1E5` and `3/4` are not automatically converted to numbers or dates.
295: - Keep the existing conservative numeric-classification behavior for values that are proven numeric.
296: 
297: ### 10.4 PDF and project edge cases
298: 
299: - Triage multiple-table and ruleless-table selections using a representative PDF sample; record prevalence and failure modes before choosing policy.
300: - Test encrypted, corrupt, unsupported, oversized, image-only and duplicate PDFs with explicit user-facing diagnostics.
301: - Test two application instances attempting to mutate or recover the same project; project-level locking must prevent concurrent writes.
302: - Establish independent reference workbooks for a representative source-PDF corpus. Expected values, cell types, destination ranges and merged ranges must be checked independently of the candidate extractor.
303: - Measure layout behavior (column widths, row heights, wrapped text, merged cells), processing latency, memory use and practical workbook-size limits before setting acceptance thresholds.
304: 
305: The initial XLSX tests described in Section 5 have now been run, and the Slint shell compiles on both CI platforms. The private-state, workbook-lock, external-edit, undo, crash-recovery, project-concurrency and broader Excel feature-preservation tests in this section remain unrun.

=== CI ===
name: Rust CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - "implementation/**"
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    name: Check (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Linux GUI build dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y pkg-config libfontconfig1-dev libreoffice-calc
      - name: Install stable Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      - name: Run workspace tests
        env:
          DH_S1_WORKBOOK_ARTIFACT: ${{ runner.temp }}/s1-empty-project.xlsx
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets
      - name: Verify project workbook opens in LibreOffice
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/s1-libreoffice-import"
          timeout 60s libreoffice --headless --convert-to ods --outdir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/s1-libreoffice-import" "${RUNNER_TEMP}/s1-empty-project.xlsx"
          test -s "${RUNNER_TEMP}/s1-libreoffice-import/s1-empty-project.ods"
      - name: Build desktop release artifact
        run: cargo build --release -p dh-app
      - name: Upload Stage 1 build and workbook artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: s1-build-${{ runner.os }}
          path: |
            target/release/dh-app*
            ${{ runner.temp }}/s1-empty-project.xlsx
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Record resolved dependency tree
        run: cargo tree --workspace -e all > phase0-cargo-tree.txt
      - name: Upload Phase 0 dependency evidence
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: phase0-dependency-evidence-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: |
            Cargo.lock
            phase0-cargo-tree.txt
          if-no-files-found: error

cargo-deny 0.22.0
Checks a project's crate graph

Usage: cargo-deny check [OPTIONS] [WHICH]...

Arguments:
  [WHICH]...
          The check(s) to perform.
          
          [possible values: advisories, bans, licenses, sources, all]

Options:
  -g, --graph <GRAPH>
          Path to graph output root directory.
          
          If set, a dotviz graph will be created for whenever multiple versions of the same crate are detected.
          
          Each file will be created at `<dir>/graph_output/<crate_name>.dot`. `<dir>/graph_output/*` is deleted and recreated each run.

      --hide-inclusion-graph
          Hide the inclusion graph when printing out info for a crate.

      --audit-compatible-output
          To ease transition from cargo-audit to cargo-deny, this flag will tell cargo-deny to output the exact same output as cargo-audit would, to `stdout` instead of `stderr`, just as with cargo-audit.
          
          Note that this flag only applies when the output format is JSON, and note that since cargo-deny supports multiple advisory databases, instead of a single JSON object, there will be 1 for each unique advisory database.

  -s, --show-stats
          Show stats for all the checks, regardless of the log-level.

  -W, --warn <WARN>
          Set lint warnings.

  -A, --allow <ALLOW>
          Set lint allowed.

  -D, --deny <DENY>
          Set lint denied.

      --feature-depth <FEATURE_DEPTH>
          Specifies the depth at which feature edges are added in inclusion graphs.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
